content.text:
I've submitted **index 5** (Bi 0.41, Cu 0.19, V 0.40) as the best composition. At **10.6 µA** it had the highest photocurrent of the three compositions I could measure, but I tested only 3 of the 149 candidates, so a better one may be unmeasured.

| Index | Composition (Bi / Cu / V) | Photocurrent | What the XRD showed |
|---|---|---|---|
| **5** | 0.41 / 0.19 / 0.40 | **10.6 µA** | Looks like BiVO4 |
| 8 | 0.46 / 0.21 / 0.33 | 6.1 µA | No XRD taken |
| 16 | 0.27 / 0.43 / 0.30 | 0 | Many phases, Cu-rich |

- **Why index 5:** BiVO4 is the known light-active compound in this system. Of all the candidates, index 5 has the closest to equal Bi and V with the least Cu, and its XRD peaks match BiVO4.
- **Cu-rich compositions:** the Cu-rich index 16 gave no current, so I didn't spend a measurement on the Cu–V-rich corner (e.g. index 91). That call rests on one data point.
- **Not tested:** compositions with more V than Bi, such as index 10 or 3. They are the most plausible remaining alternative. I chose Bi-rich index 8 for the last measurement instead, and it came in lower than index 5.

I used all 3 photocurrent measurements and 4 of the 5 XRD scans.
